Phase 73 plan: docs/phases/subagent-kit.md. Ships three cheap, write-less helpers in the tagteam Claude Code plugin (plugin/agents/): tagteam:test-runner (haiku; focused runs → counts, failing ids, failure tails; never fixes, never the full suite), tagteam:verifier (sonnet; one claim → CONFIRMED/REFUTED/UNVERIFIABLE with evidence), tagteam:explore (haiku; pointers not dumps, tagteam-aware). All: tools Bash/Read/Grep/Glob, disallowedTools Write/Edit/NotebookEdit.

Read-only enforcement (frontmatter can't set env or hooks for plugin agents — plugins-reference): a session-level PreToolUse Bash hook in plugin/hooks/hooks.json with a shell prefilter (only payloads whose agent_type starts with `tagteam:` reach Python) → `tagteam hook pre-tool-use` returns updatedInput `export TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1; <command>` (covers compound commands; idempotent); fail-closed deny when tagteam is missing or input unparseable for a kit agent. Stated limit: a helper could `unset` it; the CLI's own read-only guards do the refusing.

Contract: SKILL.md "Read-only helpers" names the kit and when to use each (rules unchanged: one full-suite run per submission; helpers never write a cycle); packaged copy + parity test + shipped-docs audit. Doctor: one line on kit availability. No pyproject change (plugin reaches users via the marketplace).

Verification: agent files pinned; hook unit tests on real-shaped input (rewrite, compound, idempotent, pass-through for non-kit and main session, deny on malformed, prefilter doesn't start Python — timed, tagteam off PATH), fail-closed without the CLI; one LIVE check in a real Claude Code session (`claude --plugin-dir plugin`): verifier's `echo $TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY` prints 1 and `tagteam cycle add` is refused. If updatedInput / agent_type prove missing live, fallback = deny unless already prefixed (agents told to prefix).

Arbiter decision (2026-09-24): NO before/after A/B — savings unmeasured at merge, said so in the closeout; measured later via `tagteam usage --by model` on real headless turns. Open for review: hook cost on every Bash call (prefilter); explore vs built-in Explore.

The three-helper scope, focused-test rule, contract parity, and live integration check are sound. The arbiter's no-A/B decision is accepted: closeout should say savings are unmeasured. No advisory standing orders or unconsumed interjections apply. Please resolve two enforcement gaps in the plan before implementation:

1. The missing-agent_type fallback cannot enforce the claimed boundary (docs/phases/subagent-kit.md:171-176). The prefilter only enters the guard when agent_type starts with tagteam:, so if that field is missing, neither the rewrite nor "deny unless already prefixed" runs. Separate unsupported updatedInput from unavailable agent identity. Either define a concrete independently identifiable fallback and test it, or explicitly make that Claude Code version unsupported for kit delegation and require a compatible version before claiming automatic enforcement. Do not present agent instructions alone as hook enforcement. Include a missing-identity fixture and record the supported Claude Code version plus observed plugin-scoped identity in the live check. Current docs confirm agent_type for subagent tool events, but the proposed fallback still needs to be logically valid: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-input-fields .

2. Cover an installed but incompatible/failing CLI, not just a missing executable (read-only enforcement section; success criterion 3). The plugin and CLI upgrade independently. The current tagteam/hook.py returns 1 for an unknown pre-tool-use subcommand. A new plugin with that old CLI therefore has tagteam on PATH but receives no rewrite; ordinary hook exit 1 is non-blocking in Claude Code. Specify that the wrapper converts CLI failure/unsupported command and absent or unusable guard output into a blocking decision (exit 2 or valid deny JSON), and require tests executing the actual shipped wrapper with an old/failing CLI and empty/invalid output. Align the plugin's minimum CLI compatibility metadata and doctor diagnosis with the release that adds the guard. Reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output .

Implementation notes, not additional scope: preserve normal Bash permission evaluation when returning updatedInput (do not auto-allow commands); preserve the other tool_input fields. A shell prefilter is reasonable, with measured process overhead reported rather than a microsecond promise, and with the Python parser deciding the actual top-level identity. Keeping a tagteam-aware, model-pinned explore helper is reasonable. No tests run for this plan-only review.
